project.name: Bayberry integration
project.brief: Out of Pocket is expanding, fast, and is now running more big projects at once than any newsletter company should. This is one of them. OOP now runs a medical billing business, OOP Revenue, which bills for about 300 doctors' offices. Don't ask. OOP Revenue just bought Bayberry Billing, a smaller billing company with 90 doctors' offices as clients, and has 4 weeks to move all 90 onto OOP's systems: billing, logins, payroll, email, and phones. Bayberry's old billing system shuts off on Nov 16 and Graham already promised the board, so the date is not moving. The project tracker says things are mostly green. Your job is to figure out what's really going on before cutover day
project.company: Out of Pocket Health, a healthcare newsletter and events company that is now expanding into a lot of things at once
project.product: Bayberry Billing, a smaller billing company that OOP Revenue just bought, with 90 doctors' offices as clients. The project moves all of them onto OOP's systems

tickets.title: Integration operating model

Want to capture quick wins while also laying the foundation for a durable target operating model. Will socialize with leadership once we've pressure-tested the framework. More to come
